facts.statement: The genus Tienosuchus was named by Young in 1949.
The type species of the genus is Tienosuchus hsiangi, described by Young in 1949.
Tienosuchus is classified as a dubious, monospecific genus of gavialoid crocodilian.
facts.quote: Tienosuchus is a dubious extinct monospecific genus of gavialoid crocodilian.

facts.statement: Tienosuchus is closely related to the genus Thoracosaurus and was traditionally placed in the subfamily Thoracosaurinae.
facts.quote: It is closely related to the genus Thoracosaurus, and has traditionally been placed in the subfamily Thoracosaurinae.

facts.statement: The subfamily Thoracosaurinae is now considered a paraphyletic assemblage of basal gavialoids rather than a true clade.
facts.quote: The subfamily is now considered to be a paraphyletic assemblage of basal gavialoids, and therefore not a true clade.

facts.statement: Fossils of Tienosuchus date to the Eocene epoch.
Tienosuchus lived between 56 and 48.07 million years ago during the Ypresian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Ypresian (56 to 48.07 million years ago)

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Tienosuchus has been recorded.

rejected.statement: Due to the low diagnostic value of its fragmentary remains, the genus is now considered a nomen dubium.
rejected.quote: Because the fragmentary remains provide little diagnostic value, the genus is now considered a nomen dubium.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'the genus is now considered a nomen dubium'

rejected.statement: The genus is known from a single tooth and some postcranial remains found in Eocene deposits in Hunan, China.
rejected.quote: It is known from a single tooth and some postcranial remains collected from Eocene deposits in Hunan, China.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'is known from a single tooth and some'
